title: Paceboard: compact scaling controls, throughput catalog, and change chronicle for fleet operators
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Fleet operators lack a compact operator surface for quickly adjusting dedicated capacity behavior and understanding historical scaling decisions. The current Console panels are fragmented: scaling knobs are in one place, throughput dashboards in another, and change history is buried in logs. This leads to slow reaction times during surges and makes root-cause analysis of cost/latency regressions tedious.

Goal: Build a consolidated "Paceboard" UI in the Console that provides: 1) compact scaling controls (per-fleet and per-operator presets) for fast manual adjustments and safe overrides; 2) a throughput catalog that surfaces recent and forecasted throughput, spike patterns, and econ impact; 3) an immutable change chronicle (human-readable audit entries + links to PRs/rollouts) with rollback/playback affordances. The surface should be usable by SREs and platform operators during incidents and for day-to-day tuning, and integrate with RBAC, canary rollouts, and the Dedicated autoscaler API.

Proposed approach: Create a new Console subpage under Fleet > Paceboard. Add a left rail with compact scaling toggles and presets, a central throughput catalog with interactive time range and breakdowns (per-model, per-route, per-operator), and a right-hand chronological chronicle panel that shows changes, approvals, and automated actions (autoscaler-suggested changes). The Paceboard will rely on existing telemetry endpoints (metrics API), the capacity intent API (for writes), and the audit-history API for immutable entries. Implement a safe rollback button that triggers an operator rollback workflow (creates a rollback intent + optional canary).
acceptance_criteria: Paceboard UI is available under Fleet > Paceboard in Console for admin and fleet-operator RBAC roles
Compact scaling controls support: target RPS, min/max nodes, burst buffer toggle, and named presets; changes create a capacity intent via the capacity intent API
Throughput catalog shows last 14 days of throughput, 95th/50th latency, cost delta estimate for toggle changes, and a forecast curve for next 24 hours
Change chronicle is append-only, shows human-readable descriptions, user, timestamp, linked PR/Runbook, and provides a one-click rollback that opens a rollback modal prefilled with previous intent
Telemetry and cost calculations are surfaced with sample size & confidence intervals; metrics page links to query builder for deep dives
E2E tests cover UI flows for making a preset change, confirming change appears in chronicle, and performing a rollback in a canary scenario
Security review checklist completed: RBAC checks, audit log retention policy, and KMS integration for any sensitive notes
steps: 1) Finalize product wireframes and edge-state behaviors with Design (Figma link in comments)
2) Define API contract with Eng for capacity intent writes and audit entries (schema + error modes)
3) Build throughput catalog backend queries and cost estimator job (reuse existing telemetry reducers)
4) Implement front-end components: paceboard shell, compact controls, catalog charting, and chronicle list
5) Integrate RBAC checks and feature-flag rollout (canary by org)
6) Add E2E and integration tests, security review, and run a small pilot with 3 customers
7) Document in Console help center and onboard SREs with runbook examples
comments: 2025-11-12 Priya Kapoor: Kickoff — scoped initial requirements after ops interviews (SRE, Platform, 2 customers). Primary ask: fewer clicks to throttle/capacity override during peak events.

2025-11-18 Olivia Brown (Design): Posted first draft wireframes in Figma (figma.com/file/abc123). Key decision: compact controls should support 'operator presets' and an 'emergency throttle' mode. Need to define preset lifecycle (who can create/delete).

2025-11-20 Rafael Ortiz (Eng): Reviewed API surface. We can reuse /capacity-intents for writes but need to extend payload to include 'operator_reason' and 'rollback_reference'. Proposed schema in github: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2890

2025-11-24 Emma Chen (Security): RBAC matrix draft attached. Recommendation: only 'fleet-operator' and above can perform rollback; 'read-only-operator' sees chronicle but cannot act. Also recommend 90-day immutable retention for chronicle entries before archival.

2025-11-27 Priya Kapoor: Trade-off note — showing cost delta inline requires near-real-time cost signals; Eng suggests using a conservative estimator for 0-1 hour forecasts and labelling as 'estimate'. Accepted for MVP with clear UI disclosure.

2025-11-30 Rafael Ortiz: Engineering spike completed. Backend changes minimal; added a new telemetry view 'paceboard_catalog' and a chronicle write endpoint. Performance note: queries default to pre-aggregated rollups to avoid dashboard slowness.

2025-12-02 Design review: Updated Figma with the chronicle micro-copy improvements and the rollback modal flow. UX tweak: confirmation requires selecting rollback reason from dropdown to encourage documentation.
2025-12-02 QA: Found a race where rapid successive preset writes can create duplicate intents. ENG to add idempotency key per operator action (ENG-12019).

2025-12-02 Priya Kapoor: Plan next — schedule a 2-week pilot with internal SREs and set up alerting on 'paceboard-change-failure' metric. Add follow-up ticket for localization and accessibility audit.
